story: The Henry Wadsworth Longfellow Monument stands on a triangular plaza at Congress and State Streets, in Portland's West End. The intersection is called Longfellow Square.
Sculptor Franklin Simmons began the design in 1885, three years after Longfellow's death, and the pedestal was designed by Francis H. Fassett. The monument was unveiled on September 29, 1888.

The bronze statue is about 7 feet (2.1 m) tall. It shows the poet late in life, seated in a chair with lion-head arms and a stack of books beneath it. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1990.

stops.disputed: Many people picture a famous poet as young. Wikipedia says the statue shows him as he looked late in life.

claims.t: The statue shows Longfellow as a young boy.
claims.why: Wikipedia says it shows him late in life.

story: Ships entering Portland's harbor could not be seen directly from the wharfs, which made it hard for merchants to prepare for cargoes. In 1807, Captain Lemuel Moody organized the construction of an observatory on Munjoy Hill.

The tower is 86 feet (26 m) tall, has seven stories, and is octagonal to lessen wind pressure. Using a telescope and signal flags, people could talk to ships hours before they reached the docks. It is the only known surviving tower of its type in the United States.
It was designated a National Historic Landmark in 2006 and is now managed by Greater Portland Landmarks as a museum.

The Observatory was built for studying stars.

story: The Wadsworth-Longfellow House was built by Revolutionary War General Peleg Wadsworth between 1785 and 1786. It was the first wholly brick dwelling in Portland and is the oldest standing structure on the Portland peninsula.
Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was born in 1807 at his aunt's house nearby. He moved into this house at eight months old and spent the next 35 years there. The Longfellows added the third story in 1815.

Anne Longfellow Pierce, the last family member to live in the house, kept it much as it was. When she died in 1901, her will gave it to the Maine Historical Society, which opened it to the public the next year.

story: Portland City Hall is the fourth city hall built in Portland. It was built between 1909 and 1912 and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.

The earlier hall, designed by Francis H. Fassett and built in 1867, burned in 1908. The one before that, built in 1862, burned in the Great Fire of 1866. The new building was designed by New York firm Carrère & Hastings, with local help from John Calvin Stevens and John Howard Stevens.

Its granite tower is 200 feet (61 m) tall. John M. Carrère, who was inspired by New York City Hall, considered it one of his finest works. The addition on Myrtle Street includes Merrill Auditorium, home of the Kotzschmar Memorial Organ.

stops.disputed: Many people assume a city hall is built once. Wikipedia says this is the fourth, after earlier ones burned.

claims.t: The current City Hall was built between 1909 and 1912.
The 1867 City Hall is the one standing today.
